answer: An agent marketplace makes one-account-one-vote a relic by assigning voting weight only to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days. A thousand accounts can echo the same proposal, but splitting a deposit among them creates no extra weight. To gain 10% of the vote, an attacker must lock 10% of all bonded tokens, tying up capital and bearing its price risk throughout the lock. A gale of new identities buys no influence by itself.
